desc:
The array nums is sorted in non-decreasing order. For every element x compute f(x) = a·x2 + b·x + c, where a, b and c are given integers. Return all the values f(x) as an array sorted in non-decreasing order.

Computing and sorting is O(n log n). Because f is a parabola (or a line when a = 0), the values can be put in order in O(n).

nums = [-4, -2, 2, 4], a = 1, b = 3, c = 5
f(x) = x^2 + 3x + 5  gives  9, 3, 15, 33
result = [3, 9, 15, 33]
hints: A parabola is decreasing on one side of its vertex and increasing on the other, so the transformed sequence is a concatenation of a descending and an ascending run. Which elements give the extreme values?
If a > 0 the parabola opens upwards: the largest values of f are at the two ends of nums and the smallest is near the vertex. If a < 0 the opposite holds.

Use two pointers at both ends. For a ≥ 0 fill the result from the back: put the larger of f(nums[l]) and f(nums[r]) at the next free back position and move that pointer inward. For a < 0 fill from the front with the smaller one.
editorial: When a > 0 the graph of f is a valley. The farther an input is from the vertex -b / 2a, the larger its output, so on the sorted input the maximum of f over any remaining stretch is at one of its two ends. Compare f at the left and right ends, write the larger into the result starting from the last slot, and move the corresponding pointer inward. After n steps the result is sorted. For a < 0 the graph is a hill, so the ends hold the smallest remaining values: fill from the front with the smaller one.

The case a = 0 is a line. It is covered by the a ≥ 0 branch: f is monotone, so the larger end value is always the right end (if b > 0) or the left end (if b < 0), and comparing the two ends still picks the correct maximum. Total work is O(n) time and O(n) output space. Magnitudes are at most 100·106 + 100·103 + 100, which fits in 32 bits.
